Economic Importance: i. The plant of the family are cultivated for vegetables. ii. Chillies are used as spices. iii. Some species are the source of valuable medicines. iv. Petunia, Datura etc. are grown as ornamental plants.

Some important plant of this family: a. Tomato – Lycopersicum esculentum b. Brinjal – Solanum melongena c. Potato – Solanum tuberosum d. Black night shade – Solanum nigrum e. Tobacco – Nicotina tabacum
Habit and Habitat : The members of this family annual, biennial and perennial herbs and shrubs. They are cosmopolitan in distribution mostly found in tropical and temperate region of the world.

Vegetative characters: a. Root: adventitious root b. Stem: herbaceous or woody, erect or climbing or sometimes modified into underground bulbs or rhizomes, branched, solid. c. Leaves: cauline or radical, exstipulate, usually simple, alternate or whorled, parallel venation, sessile with usually sheathing leaf base.
Floral Characters a. Inflorescence: racemose b. Flower: bracteate or ebracteate, bisexual, incomplete, hypogynous
c. Perianth: 6 tepals arranged in two rows, gamotapetalous rarely polytepalous, valvate or imbricate aestivation, sepaloid or petaloid
d. Androecium: 6 stamens arranged in two rows, polyandrous, epiphyllous, anther dithecous, basifixed, introrse
e. Gynoecium: 3 carpels, syncarpous, trilocular, ovary superior, axile placentation f. Fruits: fleshy berry or a capsule g. Pollination: entomophilous h. Floral Formula: i. Floral Diagram:

Economic Importance: i. Some plants are grown as ornamental in the gardens. ii. Asparagus is consumed as vegetable. iii. Some plants are of great medical value used in treatment of rheumatism and gout. iv. Aloe are used to manufacture different types of cosmetic products. v.
